name: Clips
description: A local-first video capture and ingest surface with a bundled editor preview. The out-of-process ryu-clips sidecar owns Core→Shadow recording and URL ingest; transcript-led analysis and vertical rendering are not connected yet.

permission_levels.label: Can view
permission_levels.description: Browse and play back recorded clips, including whatever was on screen when they were captured.

permission_levels.label: Can capture
permission_levels.description: Record new clips and ingest external ones, which starts screen capture on this machine.

chat_widget_templates.title: Clips widget
chat_widget_templates.description: Clips chat widget metadata is coming soon; no render tool is available yet.

hook_events.title: Clip recording started
hook_events.description: Fires when POST /api/clips/start has actually begun a capture on Shadow and a clip id exists. A start Shadow refused, or one that never reached it (the fail-soft `{ available: false }` body), does not fire. The clip has no video and no duration yet — those arrive with `clip.ready`; this is the moment to react to recording having begun (announce it, arm a timer, dim a surface).

hook_events.title: Clip ready
hook_events.description: Fires once a finished clip bundle exists — from BOTH paths that produce one: stopping a recording (POST /api/clips/{id}/stop) and completing an ingest of a watched URL or a local video file (POST /api/clips/ingest). `source` is how a consumer tells them apart; the bundle itself does not record which. Fires once per clip, alongside (not after) the auto-file into the Clips Space, so it still fires if that filing fails. `framesEndpoint` is the Core-served path, already rewritten off Shadow's internal one, so a consumer can fetch frames from it directly; the mp4 is at /api/clips/{id}/file.
